subject.title: Feature: Webchat / Control UI inline button support (buttons parameter, callback RPC, capabilities config)

question: Should WebChat inline controls use the shared `MessagePresentation` typed-action contract with an authenticated `chat.callback` RPC, and should WebChat get a persisted capability gate despite current docs retiring WebChat config?
rationale: The request adds public Gateway protocol, callback authorization semantics, Control UI behavior, and likely config/capability surface, which automation should not decide without maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Adopt shared presentation plus callback RPC
options.body: Use `MessagePresentation` typed actions, add an authenticated Gateway callback path, and explicitly defer webhook/zero-token bypass unless separately approved.

options.title: Split contract and UI delivery
options.body: First land a maintainer-reviewed protocol/capability design, then implement Control UI rendering and click handling against that contract.

options.title: Avoid persisted WebChat config
options.body: Expose WebChat inline controls through client negotiation or a non-persisted capability path instead of reviving retired WebChat config keys.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared presentation plus callback RPC
recommendation.body: Use `MessagePresentation` typed actions, add an authenticated Gateway callback path, and explicitly defer webhook/zero-token bypass unless separately approved.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is recent Control UI chat work and current renderer ownership evidence.
